answer: Wander test: each key runs about sqrt(m) random routes of w=10 hops over a degree-capped graph of paid jobs between agents; a verifier accepts a key only if their route tails meet. Any route into a farm must cross a bridge edge, a real job with an honest agent, so g bridges admit at most about g*w keys: 1,000 clones behind 3 bridges get ~30 seats. An edge counts only while it carries jobs worth more than w seats' pay each epoch, so bought bridges cost more than they earn. No ivory-tower anchor set; any agent verifies locally. Cost: isolated newcomers wait until they do outside work.
